Magicians are the summoners of the arcane arts, and wield the power to call forth everything from a loaf of bread to a huge Fire Elemental
to fight for them. While not as adept at offensive spells as the Wizards, Magicians still wield considerable power in this area as well. - EverQuest manual = Description = [[File:C magician.gif|right]] Magicians are master summoners, able to call elemental pets to do their bidding and to conjure useful items from thin air. Magicians are primarily a magic-using class, with the ability to wear cloth armor and wield blunt weapons and daggers. Elemental pets are at the heart of a magician's offensive strategy, and typically accompany a magician in all his adventures. This pet provides protection for its master, along with powerful attacks and special abilities. Magicians have a large selection of fire and magic-based damage spells, allowing them to mount a damaging magical assault in support of their elemental pet. Magicians have a wide range of summoning spells, allowing them to conjure such diverse items as food, weapons, armor, and magical jewelry. In battle, the magician can encase his entire group in a shield of fire, damaging any opponent that strikes them. Magicians also have spells that lower a monster's resistance to magic, allowing spells to damage them more easily. Magicians are a very focused class, sacrificing some diversity for power in their area of expertise. Magicians are able to adventure solo, but also provide value in a group situation. The magician is a good choice for players who enjoy managing a powerful pet and using a tightly focused spell selection. === Class Titles === In the original [[Kunark]] expansion, classes would gain new titles at levels over 50. In EverQuest Legends, these titles are not available, and it is unknown how they will be presented. Mages are the least strength dependant class in the game. They don't melee past the very first few levels and they have a way easier time time carrying loot with their weightless and 100% weight reducing bags that they can summon. *'''Stamina''' - Gives a minor increase in maximum Hit Points. Each tier of pet summoning spells has 4 types; one for each elemental magic. Massive amounts of information on each of the types can be found below the list of spells. === Single Target Direct Damage === Pretty self-explanatory. While magicians don't get the efficiency or elemental array of direct damage attacks that wizards do, what they do get is comparable until the wizard lure line of spells. Magicians have two types of direct damage spells: fire-based and magic-based. Interestingly, the magic-based damage spells use Conjuration, while the fire-based ones use Evocation. === Projectile Direct Damage === Projectile, or 'Bolt' spells cast a ball (of fire, in the magicians case) that travels fairly quickly from the caster to the target. These tend to do more damage, have longer range (the base range of a bolt is 300' whereas the standard range for DDs is 200'), and have better efficiency than similar level non-projectile DD spells, but the bolt type of spell has its drawbacks as well. First, bolts can be "lost" if the region has a lot of elevation changes. It is best to make sure you are at the same elevation as the mob with no intervening terrain features. If the surrounding area does not allow for that, having a decent distance and higher elevation helps the spell land (and it also looks great to have your lava bolt drop like a bomb). The second drawback is that the bolt can and will hit mobs that are directly in between you and the mob you are aiming at (this is not true anymore on EQ live and therefore probably on EQL). === Target-Based Area of Effect === Mages have two types of target-based AoE fire spells: "columns" and "rains". PBAoE spells will hit up to 8 targets. Targeted AoE will hit up to 4 targets. === Player-Based Area of Effect === In EQL, players who cast AOE spells do not hurt themselves, their party, their pet, other NPCs that are not in combat such as guards, and it does not break mez. They will also deal the killing blow if targets get low enough on health. AOE damage spells are limited to hitting 8 targets max. === Damage Shields === A magician's damage shield is one of the best in the game, second only to a Bard with the appropriate instrument (and your pre-50+ Fire or Epic pet's innate DS). Although it is fire-based, it is unresistable, and depending on what you or your group are fighting, can be the #1 source of damage in a battle. There are not many situations a magician will find themselves in where casting a DS will NOT be worth it. === Malo Line === Magicians and Shamans have a debuff line of spells that lower the Cold, Fire, Magic, and Poison resists of whatever it's cast on. Magicians get these spells a few levels after Shamans, but the spells themselves are identical except for the last one in the line. Shamans get the unresistable Malo (-45) and Magicians get the somewhat less powerful unresistable Mala (-35). Both of these have a lower resist debuff, a longer casting time and a higher mana cost than the highest resistable counterpart (at -60). Note that, aside from those last two, the spells themselves do not have a negative resist modifier, so can be hard to land on higher level mobs. In a group situation with an Enchanter, the Tash line is often used first to help the Malo line land and together can help anyone land their spells more effectively. === Summoned Items === While the number of different items magicians can summon is immense (it is their primary class identifier, after all...), all summoned items are NO RENT. In other words, they will not persist when you log out. To prevent the loss of items (especially in summoned bags) due to link death, there is a ~15 minute grace period, but if you plan on logging for the night, do NOT forget to unload your summoned bags! However, a summoned weapon or armor part (starting in Luclin era, magicians can summon tradable armor and focus jewelry) given to a pet stays permanently on the pet until it dies or the pet owner forces his pet to destroy it. {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! Once magicians get a decent main hand weapon for themselves, though, most summoned weapons are relegated to pet use only. Weapons can be given to pets at the lowest levels to make sure they can damage monsters that are immune to mundane weaponry, just like for yourself (or group-mates). Also, at low levels, and before pets get dual wield, the summoned 2H staves' damage will be a bit higher than the pet's innate melee damage. Once pets get the innate ability to damage magical creatures, weapons can be used to allow them to dual wield. There is an argument to be made for giving them the Spear of Warding and a Dagger of Symbols for the resists, but +5 is not a lot.
